name: Paroxetine Hydrochloride
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride hemihydrate), slightly soluble in water.
On the WHO List of Essential Medicines; one of the most commonly prescribed antidepressants worldwide. First approval/introduction: US FDA 1992 (GlaxoSmithKline).

Highly potent selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor with modest muscarinic receptor affinity. Receptor / target profile: The most potent SSRI at SERT (Ki 0.07–0.2 nM); weaker NET inhibition and modest muscarinic affinity.
Extensive hepatic, mostly CYP2D6 (saturable; potent CYP2D6 inhibitor)
Summary: Completely absorbed; controlled-release form gives Tmax 6–10 h. ~95% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2D6 (saturable, non-linear kinetics); potent CYP2D6 inhibitor. Half-life ~21 h.
Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia
Depression: 25 mg once daily; increase by 12.5 mg weekly; max 62.5 mg/day
Panic disorder: 12.5 mg once daily; max 75 mg/day
Social anxiety: 12.5 mg once daily; max 37.5 mg/day
Elderly / severe renal or hepatic impairment: start 12.5 mg; max 50 mg/day
Swallow whole, usually in the morning; taper slowly when stopping
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
CrCl <30: start 12.5 mg CR; max 50 mg/day.
Severe impairment: start 12.5 mg CR; max 50 mg/day.
Start 12.5 mg CR; max 50 mg/day; anticholinergic effects.
Not recommended (lack of efficacy, suicidality signal).
First-trimester exposure associated with increased risk of cardiac malformations – avoid if possible.
Low milk levels; use with caution.

Discontinuation syndrome is common – taper slowly
Congenital cardiac defects (if used in early pregnancy)
CYP2D6 substrates – TCAs, risperidone, metoprolol, tamoxifen (reduced efficacy)
With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Nausea, vomiting, tremor, mydriasis, dry mouth, sweating, somnolence, serotonin syndrome. Supportive care.
Cipriani et al., Lancet 2018 – effective but with higher discontinuation symptoms.
Paroxetine CR trials (Golden et al., 2002) – efficacy in MDD with lower early discontinuation than IR.
Never stop suddenly – taper with your doctor
May cause drowsiness and weight gain
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
